correctness.rationale: The exact lower-triangular coefficients follow from the Bergman power kernel. Contour rotation of the complex moment integral to angle π/4 yields a unique nondegenerate saddle at scaled coordinate one and an explicit first correction, which gives the correct amplitude, phase and stretched-exponential decay. Small- and large-ray tails are exponentially dominated. Each row is a rank-one operator of stretched-exponentially summable norm, establishing every Schatten quasi-ideal. Finite compressions establish the Fredholm determinant and eigenvalue multiset by trace-norm convergence. A bounded-variation integration-by-parts argument justifies the conditionally convergent incomplete-Gamma trace. Positive variation gives coefficients n^(α+1−s), never square summable for α>−1, 0<s<1/2. CHECK.py ran successfully with 37 finite assertions; no finite test was used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating Bergman-kernel theory rests on a positivity hypothesis: the natural total-variation control here is maximally misleading, failing even H² image of the constant, while exact complex-phase cancellations yield every Schatten quasi-ideal. The precise universal moment asymptotics are not a renaming of a standard boundedness test; they give the entire nonzero spectrum and a Gamma-function trace invariant independent of the kernel parameter. This is a motivated structural boundary for positivity-based operator criteria, rather than an arbitrary finite calculation.
